verdict.rationale: Obsidian exposes a plugin API (Vault interface for files/folders) and an Obsidian URI scheme for triggering actions like opening/creating notes, and its plain-Markdown storage means most content operations can be scripted outside the UI. However, this is a local plugin/URI surface, not a full first-party API that mirrors every UI capability (e.g., Sync, Publish, settings management aren't shown as API-controllable), and plugins by default have no sandboxing, meaning power comes from unrestricted filesystem/HTTP access rather than a designed parity API. Missing for 10: an official comprehensive REST/programmatic API covering Sync/Publish/settings, and evidence of AI-native or headless full UI-parity workflows beyond file/URI manipulation.
